title: request-latency-heatmap-and-context-staleness-detector
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview:
Introduce a lightweight SDK instrumentation hook that emits request-level latency heatmap buckets and detects 'context staleness' (cases where request context/kv cache is unexpectedly reused across logical requests). The goal is to provide an early warning signal for instrumentation regressions that manifest as inflated tail latency or incorrect attribution in traces.

Success criteria:
- SDK hook can be enabled via config flag in JS/Go/Python SDKs with <1% p50 CPU overhead in our microbenchmark.
- Heatmap metrics (10ms/25/50/100/250/500/1000+/count) emitted per route and model variant to metrics pipeline.
- Staleness detector emits events when a request's context fingerprint matches a recent request but timestamps diverge (configurable window).
- Dashboard and alerting recipe in Console: heatmap per-route and a 'staleness spike' alert (SLO: alert <3 false positives/day).

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We avoid full-span enrichment at high QPS to keep overhead low: the hook uses a tiny in-memory rolling sampler that records coarse buckets and a compact 64-bit fingerprint for context identity.
- Sampling: default 1% continuous sampling for heatmap buckets, plus an opportunistic tail-sampler that captures 100% of requests exceeding the 95th latency percentile for the route. This balances signal without high cardinality.
- Context staleness detection uses an adaptive TTL per route; shorter TTLs for high-concurrency routes. This reduces cross-request false positives but requires tuning.
- Compatibility: exposes OTEL semantic attributes and a bridging shim so existing ingest pipelines accept metrics & events.

Implementation plan:
1) SDK core: small C/Go/TS module that records per-request duration into coarse buckets and emits a compact metric envelope. (MARCO)
2) Context fingerprint: deterministic canonicalization of the request envelope (method, route, model, truncated prompt hash) -> 64-bit hash. Keep stable across SDK versions. (ASHA + MARCO)
3) Staleness detector: local LRU cache of recent fingerprints with last-seen timestamps and sequence counters for streaming requests. Emit event if reused fingerprint with last-seen older than route TTL. (MARCO)
4) Metrics export: format compatible with our existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus and protobuf envelope path) + OTEL translation. (ENG-METRICS)
5) Console: add heatmap widget for route-level latency percentiles and a staleness event timeline; wire alerting rule template. (PM/Console)
6) Rollout: opt-in controlled flag, gradual rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary dashboards.

Testing & benchmarks:
- Microbench harness created under infra/benchmarks/latency-heatmap to validate <1% CPU overhead at 50k rps.
- Integration test: run against staging tracing pipeline and verify OTEL attribute mapping and metric count preservation.
- Fault injection: simulate wrapped request contexts (deliberate reuse) to validate detection and false-positive rate.

Telemetry/observability outputs:
- Metric names: redwood.request.latency_heatmap.bucket, labels: route, model, env, bucket
- Events: redwood.request.context_staleness with payload: fingerprint, route, last_seen_ts, current_ts, sample_trace_id
- Trace enrichment: when a staleness event fires we include sample_trace_id pointing to a captured trace at tail-sampler.

Security & privacy:
- Fingerprint created from truncated one-way SHA256 over permitted request metadata; no raw prompt text stored.
- Security review required (PII gating) before >50% rollout.

Dashboard/alerting:
- Console widgets: per-route heatmap, 95/99th time series, and staleness event rate.
- Alert recipe: staleness_rate > threshold (route-specific) sustained for 5m -> PagerDuty. Default threshold tuned to avoid noisy alerts.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/observability/latency-heatmap-design-v1
- Benchmarks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/heatmap-bench
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 (WIP)
- Console ticket: PM-7981 (dashboard + alerting)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- TTL heuristic for staleness per-route: start with 10s for low-QPS routes, 2s for high-QPS. Need SRE input.
- Should fingerprint include model_version? Including makes detection precise for model rollouts but increases cardinality for multi-model routes.

Next steps:
- Finish SDK core instrumentation and baseline microbench (target: 2026-03-18).
- Add OTEL shim and validate metrics ingestion in staging (2026-03-21).
- Create Console heatmap widget draft and alert recipe (PM + Console Eng) (2026-03-24).

Notes on uniqueness: this ticket focuses on combining coarse heatmap metrics with a novel 'context staleness' detector (to catch instrumentation regressions and cross-request context leaks), rather than pure span propagation work. Intentionally keeps overhead low and ties to tail sampling for deep investigation traces.
